questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant deployment patterns, including per-tenant isolation, feature flag management, and automated quality gates in enterprise environments.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- AKS with per-tenant namespaces
- App Configuration for feature flags
- k6 synthetic testing
- Azure Monitor logging
- Per-tenant promotion gates with automated rollback

## Code Example

```yaml
name: MultiTenantCanary
trigger: none
stages:
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployTenant
    strategy:
      matrix:
        tenantA: { tenant: 'tenant-a' }
        tenantB: { tenant: 'tenant-b' }
    environment: 'aks-${tenant}'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Deploy to AKS namespace'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --resource-group $(rgName) --name $(aksCluster)
                kubectl set image deployment/api api=$(containerImage) --namespace=$(tenant)
          - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
            displayName: 'Fetch feature flags'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              appConfigurationResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              appConfigurationName: '$(appConfigName)'
              label: '$(tenant)'
          - task: Bash@3
            displayName: 'Run k6 synthetic tests'
            env:
              TENANT_URL: 'https://$(tenant).api.example.com'
            inputs:
              filePath: 'tests/k6-synthetic.sh'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Check health and gate promotion'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s https://$(tenant).api.example.com/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed for $(tenant)"
                  exit 1
                fi
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Rollback on failure'
            condition: failed()
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                kubectl rollout undo deployment/api --namespace=$(tenant)
                echo "Rolled back $(tenant) to previous revision"
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
            inputs:
              azureResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              resourceType: 'Container Insights'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to compose a practical, end‑to‑end CI/CD flow for a Python service: containerization, multi-environment deployment, feature flags, secret management, manual gates, health validation, and observability.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines and stages
- Docker build and push to Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- Deployment slots for staging and prod
- Azure App Configuration per environment for feature flags
- Azure Key Vault integration for test secrets
- Manual approvals and post‑deploy health checks
- Automatic rollback and Log Analytics auditing

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
variables:
  imageName: 'python-microservice'
  registry: 'myacr.azurecr.io'
stages:
- stage: BuildTest
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    steps:
    - checkout: self
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs: { versionSpec: '3.x' }
    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
      displayName: 'Install dependencies'
    - script: |
        pytest
      displayName: 'Run tests'
    - script: |
        ruff . --select M,R
      displayName: 'Lint'
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerregistry: '$(registry)'
        repository: '$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: '$(Build.BuildId)'
- stage: DeployStaging
  dependsOn: BuildTest
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployStg
    environment: 'staging'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: |
              echo Deploying to staging slot
            displayName: 'Deploy to staging'
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs:
              appName: 'my-app-staging'
              images: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
- stage: ProdGate
  dependsOn: DeployStaging
  jobs:
  - job: ApproveProd
    steps:
    - task: ManualValidation@0
      inputs:
        notifyUsers: '['user@domain.com']'
        timeout: '0:30:00'
        title: 'Approve prod deployment'
        instructions: 'Review health and metrics before production deployment'
- stage: DeployProd
  dependsOn: ProdGate
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployProd
    environment: 'production'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: |
              echo Deploying to production slot
            displayName: 'Deploy to prod'
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs:
              appName: 'my-app-production'
              images: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
          - script: |
              curl -sSf http://my-app-production/health
            displayName: 'Post-deploy health check'
          - powershell: |
              $healthy = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://my-app-production/health' -UseBasicParsing).StatusCode -eq 200
              if (-not $healthy) { throw 'Health check failed' }
            displayName: 'Health verification'
- stage: RollbackIfNeeded
  dependsOn: DeployProd
  condition: failed()
  jobs:
  - job: Rollback
    steps:
    - script: |
        echo Rolling back to previous prod image
      displayName: 'Rollback'
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for per-tenant feature flags?
- What changes would you make to improve observability and auditability?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of end-to-end CD basics: source → build → test → containerize → push → deploy with kubectl; environment-specific config and secrets integration; security gates and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- AKS deployment via kubectl
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment settings
- Azure Key Vault for secrets
- Image vulnerability scanning gate
- Post-deploy health checks and rollback
- Logging to Azure Monitor Logs

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
steps:
- task: NodeTool@0
  inputs:
    versionSpec: '16.x'
- script: |
    npm ci
    npm test
  displayName: 'Install and test'
- task: Docker@2
  inputs:
    containerRegistry: '$(ACRServiceConnection)'
    repository: 'node-api'
    command: 'buildAndPush'
    Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
    tags: |
      $(Build.BuildId)
- task: Kubernetes@1
  inputs:
    connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
    azureSubscription: '$(AZ_SUBSCRIPTION)'
    azureResourceGroup: 'rg'
    kubernetesCluster: 'cluster'
    namespace: 'default'
    command: 'apply'
    useConfigurationFile: true
    configuration: |
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: node-api
      spec:
        replicas: 1
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: node-api
              image: <ACR>/node-api:$(Build.BuildId)
              ports:
              - containerPort: 3000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this for multi-tenant deployments with per-tenant namespaces?
- How would you implement a manual approval gate before production deployment?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design multi-tenant infra with per-tenant isolation, policy gating, drift validation, automated cleanup, and centralized logging.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant Terraform provisioning (RGs, VNets, App Services)
- Policy gates (Azure Policy + OPA) per tenant
- Drift checks against repo/ARM state before prod
- Per-tenant end-to-end tests and automated cleanup
- Centralized logging to Azure Monitor and dashboards

## Code Example

```javascript
# Illustrative YAML snippet (pseudo)
trigger:
- main
stages:
- stage: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: Terraform
    steps:
    - script: terraform init
    - script: terraform apply -var 'tenant_id=${TENANT_ID}'
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle partial promotion if a subset of tenants fail tests?
- How would you verify and guard against drift after a production upgrade?
